answer: My pick is a weather-sensor anchor. Each agent mounts a $35 sensor in a copper housing, logging temperature, humidity, pressure hourly, each reading signed. Readings must mirror the three nearest stations within half a degree and 2 percent humidity, in a meadow or on karst rock. Spot checks demand a fresh reading in ten minutes, catching every whisper of wind, from ember afternoons to cold snaps. A miss freezes the identity and burns a 250 POA bond. Faking 1,000 agents needs 1,000 sensors in 1,000 climates, $35,000 in hardware plus $12,000 a month hosting. One roof, one sky, one agent.
